status: Prepared for discussion only. Not executed or tested.
title: A payment supported by a fictional agreement and invoice
rationale: Unlike the regular-payments case, this case supplies documents describing a payment purpose. Check whether agents use that evidence without treating the documents as proof that all activity is legitimate.
reading_guide: Start with input: it describes the payment and a simulated model alert.
Then read additional_evidence: these are fictional document excerpts, not evaluation instructions or real attachments.
Finally read evaluation: these are expectations for the reviewer and must never be sent to the model as evidence.
integration_note: This draft is not registered in CASE_NAMES or the experiment runner. The current build_case_context accepts transaction and model fields but does not load these additional document records. Before executing this case, explicitly connect additional_evidence to CaseContext without passing evaluation or reading notes. No loader change is included in this task.

additional_evidence.reference: Fictional agreement SYN-AGREEMENT-04, payment terms excerpt
additional_evidence.description: The supplied agreement states that Customer 04 will pay Service Provider 04 a monthly fee of 1200 USD for bookkeeping services. It identifies bank-A:customer-04 as the payer account and bank-B:provider-04 as the recipient account. The fee for August 2022 is due on 2022-09-08.

additional_evidence.reference: Fictional invoice SYN-INVOICE-04, payment details excerpt
additional_evidence.description: The supplied invoice, issued on 2022-09-01 by Service Provider 04 to Customer 04, requests 1200 USD for August 2022 bookkeeping services under SYN-AGREEMENT-04. Payment is due on 2022-09-08 from bank-A:customer-04 to bank-B:provider-04.

prosecution: Acknowledge that the agreement and invoice give a documented payment purpose consistent with the supplied transaction amount, currency, account pair and payment date.
Do not ignore the documents or invent a suspicious explanation merely to defend the alert.
Explain that the simulated model alert is a review signal, not proof of wrongdoing; no model reasons were supplied.
Identify any remaining verification as an information gap, not evidence of misconduct.
defense: Explain that a bookkeeping-service payment is supported by supplied document excerpts, rather than being a guess based only on regularity.
Compare the actual transaction with the documented amount, currency, payer account, recipient account and due date.
Cite the relevant transaction fields AND document-04-agreement-payment-terms and document-04-invoice-payment-details when making the document-to-payment comparison.
Distinguish a documented stated purpose from independently verified authenticity, ownership or delivery of services.
forbidden: Declare proven innocence or a confirmed false positive.
Claim that the documents were authenticated or the services were independently verified.
Treat the alert record and the matching transaction as two payments.
Claim a history of monthly payments: only one transaction is supplied.
Treat the two documents as independent verification or infer why the model flagged the payment.
limitations: All accounts, documents and model values are fictional.
The excerpts document a stated purpose; authenticity and service delivery have not been checked.
Complete account history, independent ownership checks and model reasons are unavailable.
This case has not been executed. Its document-to-context integration remains to be implemented and checked after reviewing the new preprocessing interface.
